ideas.title: Indonesia Corruption Watch website
ideas.why: Information about corruption cases is often scattered across news reports, court records, government releases, and watchdog publications. A structured, searchable, source-linked website could make public-interest information easier to follow and compare over time.
ideas.idea:
Create a public-facing website focused on corruption monitoring in Indonesia, making corruption-related cases, actors, institutions, timelines, public records, and supporting sources easier to explore and understand.

The product direction is a visual, public-friendly corruption data observatory rather than a text-heavy case database. It should make complex public data understandable through moving counters, maps, timelines, charts, actor/case pages, and a continuously updated activity/news layer.
ideas.aiNotes:
Captured from the user's brain dump request on 24 Sep 2026. Initial exploration considered an independent civic-tech database, a visualization layer over public records, and a source-linked corruption knowledge graph.

Project framing was expanded after discussion: the core experience should be highly visual and understandable to the general public, including animated data counters, an Indonesia map, timelines, actors, self-updating public-source news, and aggregate figures derived only from known internet-accessible evidence.

Important interpretation rule: discovered/publicly recorded corruption is not equivalent to all corruption that exists. Every ranking, map, total, and headline metric must state exactly what it measures and its coverage.

ideas.title: Problem-mining and opportunity discovery system
ideas.why: Idea generation is often biased toward interesting solutions rather than recurring problems with real economic value. A disciplined problem-mining pipeline can improve the quality of what gets explored.
ideas.idea: Build a repeatable system that collects many real problem statements, narrows them, generates solution ideas, eliminates weak options, and keeps a smaller shortlist using structured fields such as user, problem, payer, frequency, market size, competition, difficulty, and potential.
ideas.aiNotes: Migrated from prior research workflow design.

ideas.title: Cross-tool memory wallet for AI context
ideas.why: Useful context is currently fragmented across assistants and tools. A portable memory layer could reduce repeated setup and let users carry durable context between AI products.
ideas.idea: Create a portable “memory wallet” that connects sources such as Google Drive or Notion and lets the same context be reused across AI tools through MCP, browser extensions, shortcuts, coding-agent plugins, and a developer API.

ideas.title: BarangPas as an independent product curator
ideas.why: Consumers often face noisy affiliate recommendations and unclear incentives. A consistent research and curation standard could create more trust and a stronger long-term brand.
ideas.idea: Develop BarangPas as a trust-based independent product-curation media brand for Indonesian consumers, closer to a local Wirecutter/RTINGS-style model than a generic affiliate account.
ideas.aiNotes: Migrated from prior BarangPas strategy conversations.

ideas.title: XTRA HANTU — Paste 300 Link Detector
ideas.why: Affiliate links can silently lose commission eligibility while still appearing valid, and checking large link sets manually is slow and easy to miss. The intended “magic moment” is paste → useful result in under 30 seconds.
ideas.idea: A one-page tool where a faceless affiliate can paste roughly 100–300 Shopee/Lynk.id links and quickly detect which links have lost XTRA eligibility.
ideas.aiNotes: Migrated from prior product ideation. Scope intentionally kept to the simplest one-page detector concept.

ideas.title: On-demand shift-work matching
ideas.why: Short-term labor demand and worker availability are often highly time-sensitive, but existing hiring workflows are too slow for immediate operational needs.
ideas.idea: Create an on-demand matching product for temporary or shift-based labor — essentially a “Grab for shift work” — for needs such as night shifts, seasonal demand, and events.
ideas.aiNotes: Migrated from prior project research. Kept separate from PON because it can be validated as a narrower product wedge.

ideas.title: Productive Opportunity Network
ideas.why: Many productive opportunities fail to connect because demand, available capacity, location, requirements, constraints, and economic value are fragmented across different channels.
ideas.idea: Build a Productive Opportunity Network that matches available capacity with productive demand across people ↔ employers and businesses/sellers ↔ buyers.
ideas.aiNotes: Migrated from prior project research. Core framing preserved: available capacity ↔ productive demand.

ideas.title: Per-idea history and lifecycle
ideas.why: History makes Brain Dump useful as a memory of how ideas developed, not just a list of their current state. It should live inside each idea rather than becoming another sidebar destination.
ideas.idea: Show a compact history inside each idea so the user can see how it evolved over time, for example Captured → Exploring → Pinned → Promising.
ideas.aiNotes: Migrated from prior Brain Dump project conversations on 24 Sep 2026. The user preferred History over Related/Connections.

ideas.title: Pinned ideas in Brain Dump
ideas.why: As Brain Dump grows, useful ideas can disappear in the chronological feed. Pinning gives the user a deliberate way to keep an idea in sight without relying on scoring or AI.
ideas.idea: Add a lightweight Pinned state so important ideas can stay visible without turning them into projects.
ideas.aiNotes: Migrated from prior Brain Dump project conversations on 24 Sep 2026. Wording was condensed while preserving the original intent.
